title: Breastfeeding vs formula: fed is best
summary: Both paths can nourish a healthy baby. Your family's reality matters more than labels.
whatsNormal:
Breast milk, formula, or a combination can meet your baby's needs when feeds are adequate and baby is growing.

• Breastfeeding: frequent feeds build supply; cluster feeding is common early on
• Formula: measured volumes can feel clearer; prepared safely per label instructions
• Combo feeding is valid, many families use both
• Hunger cues: rooting, hands to mouth, sucking motions, feed on cues in early weeks

There is no moral scoreboard. Hydration, weight gain, and a supported parent matter most.
watchFor: Fewer wet diapers than expected after day 4
Very long feeds every time with no satisfied periods
Excessive weight loss after the first week of life
Parent exhaustion or distress around every feed, support helps
callDoctorIf: Signs of dehydration or no wet diapers for 12+ hours after day 3
You want a lactation consult or formula guidance, your pediatrician can refer or advise
You feel pressured or guilty, talk to your clinician; feeding should not break you
